title.narrative: 24M TIC - Pilot test for the ecologically sustainable in-situ remediation of sulphuric acid mine drainage in Mpumalanga - South Africa

description.narrative: The objective is to develop feasible and sustainable solutions to reduce the environmental impacts and unleash the intrinsic social and economic values. This involves developing, testing, and comparing methodologies for the biophysical and monetary valuation of ecosystem services in the connected aquatic ecosystems such as groundwater, surface runoff and the Brugspruit river system by combining research and innovation to improve long term water security. The Sensatec business model includes (1) Study and research elements which are invoiced per daily rates for personnel and varying fees for activities; (2) Project implementations and operations which consist of sales or rental of technologies and equipment, sales of consumables as well as service fees for operational, scientific and monitoring activities. Sensatec customers range from governmental entities, through petrochemical companies to industrial and mining companies. The Sensatec value proposition includes a reliable result (experience and track record), very competitive costing (water doesn't usually need to be abstracted or soil excavated), and low energy consumption, carbon footprint, and physical footprint. In this proposed pilot project, the suitability of in-situ remediation will be researched and tested in the coal mining environment. Due to the anticipated competitive costing compared to alternatives, the method is expected to play an important role in restoration of the severely mining impacted areas.
